_comment: The curated real-cause pool. Every value here was read out of LawBase_Design on
2026-10-14, not carried over from notes. See TESTING_RULES.md rules 1, 2 and 5

swapped, and 'last_verified' is only moved forward by an actual passing health run.

pool.why: Richest fixture: all four flows have their own TAXLIT13 row on this one case, it carries the Constable + TxSecretaryState ServeBy values on TAXLIT2A 131142/131115 (the only rows in Design that reach those citation-service branches), and its two person defendants are the Maria/Cynthia Willis pair that the defendant name-split rule was derived from. Exercises the harris:dc -> harris:dccv270 court redirect.

PJ's original known-good cause. 11 plaintiffs (4 Plaintiff + 7 Intervenor Plaintiff) and a defendant re-cited under 9 AKA spelling variants, so it stresses party grouping and the exact-match 'HARRIS COUNTY' fee-party resolver far harder than a simple case does.

The only pool case where Harris County is genuinely NOT already a party, so it is the one that exercises Interventions' real first-intervention path (NewParty1 + REFERENCE, Tyler minting a new party id) instead of re-declaring an existing party.

RETIRED - do not reactivate without re-probing. Filed fine on 2026-10-01 (envelopes 328161/328162/328163), then Tyler stage lost its party data with no code change on our side: GetCase returns 'Error creating a reader for the MTOM message' and no CASEPARTYID at all. Kept here as the documented precedent that a known-good cause can rot.

NOT USABLE AS-IS. Recorded in the plan as the multi-petition fee fixture ($878.68 / two $350 petitions), but that observation was made in LawBase_Sandbox - in Design this case has no TAXLIT13 rows at all. A multi-petition fee fixture still needs to be built in Design before PLB-1248 can assert on fee math; this entry exists so the gap is not silently forgotten.
